title: Building a Ranch-Style Concurrent Acceptor Pool & gen_tcp:controlling_process/2 Handoff
solutionExplanation:
### Solution Breakdown: High-Concurrency Socket Handoff
1. **Controlling Process Transfer**: `gen_tcp:controlling_process(ClientSocket, WorkerPid)` assigns the worker as the designated port owner before any data packets are read.
2. **Readiness Signal**: After handoff succeeds, the acceptor transmits `{socket_ready, ClientSocket}` to awaken the worker thread.
3. **Concurrent Acceptor Loops**: Spawning multiple processes that call `gen_tcp:accept(ListenSocket)` concurrently allows the operating system kernel to distribute incoming connections across CPU cores with zero synchronization locks.

otpDocCards.description: Assigns a new controlling process to the socket. All subsequent events are delivered to Pid.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Transfers port ownership in O(1) time.

otpDocCards.description: Accepts an incoming TCP connection request on a listening socket descriptor.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Blocks caller until a client completes the 3-way handshake.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why must the ListenSocket be opened in passive mode ({active, false}) when using an acceptor pool with connection workers?
mentalModelCheck.codeSnippet:
ListenOpts = [binary, {packet, raw}, {active, false}, {reuseaddr, true}],
{ok, ListenSocket} = gen_tcp:listen(Port, ListenOpts).

options.label: If the socket were active, incoming client data would arrive in the acceptor process's mailbox before gen_tcp:controlling_process/2 finishes transferring ownership to the newly spawned worker.
options.explanation: Precisely! By keeping the socket in passive mode during handshake and handoff, incoming data waits safely in OS kernel buffers until the worker is spawned, takes ownership, and explicitly arms {active, once}.

options.label: Passive mode is required by the Linux kernel to support multiple CPU cores.
options.explanation: Linux supports active sockets across all cores; the passive requirement is an Erlang concurrency handoff invariant.

options.label: Active mode sockets cannot be closed by a supervisor.
options.explanation: Supervisors can close any socket descriptor regardless of active mode.
